package_info.package_versions: All IPFS deployments since January 1, 2024 (exact commit/version not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: A developer surreptitiously inserted malicious JavaScript into the Tornado Cash frontend, which covertly exfiltrated users’ private deposit notes to an attacker-controlled server. This enabled the attacker to steal funds by reconstructing users' withdrawal credentials. The attack was a supply chain compromise, hidden within a governance proposal, and specifically targeted users accessing the app via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user initiates a deposit or withdrawal action in the Tornado Cash UI
execution_context.file_location: JavaScript frontend code, within the deposit/withdrawal handler functions (e.g., main app logic handling user transactions)
required_permissions: Access to in-memory deposit notes (private cryptographic secrets/keys)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions, the code reads the user's private deposit note, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in the exfiltration of sensitive credentials and enabling theft of user funds.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive deposit notes (which function as private keys) and transmits them to an external, attacker-controlled server. This behavior is highly suspicious in a privacy-focused application, as it directly undermines user security and privacy.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets to any third-party server. All sensitive operations and secrets must remain strictly client-side to preserve user privacy and security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might send anonymized, non-sensitive usage data (such as page views or error logs), but never private keys, deposit notes, or any cryptographic secrets.
key_indicators: Network request (e.g., fetch or XMLHttpRequest) to an untrusted, non-official external domain during sensitive operations
Access and encoding of private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets within transaction handlers
Exfiltration logic embedded in deposit/withdrawal code paths
Absence of such network requests in official, uncompromised Tornado Cash frontend code

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is covertly merged into the Tornado Cash frontend codebase via a deceptive governance proposal, introducing credential exfiltration logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the deployed frontend and distributed via IPFS gateways.

attack_chain.action: Users access the compromised Tornado Cash UI through public IPFS gateways (such as ipfs.io or cf-ipfs.com), unknowingly loading the malicious frontend code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript executes in users' browsers during normal app usage.

attack_chain.action: When users perform deposit or withdrawal actions, the malicious code captures their private deposit notes and prepares them for exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Private deposit notes are transmitted to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: The attacker receives the exfiltrated deposit notes and uses them to reconstruct withdrawal credentials, enabling unauthorized withdrawal of user funds.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of user funds and compromise of user privacy.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in DeFi UIs that reads or accesses private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets and sends them to external servers during deposit or withdrawal operations
Unexpected network requests (e.g., fetch, XMLHttpRequest) to non-official or untrusted domains triggered by user-initiated financial actions
Obfuscated or hidden logic embedded within transaction handler functions (e.g., deposit/withdrawal) that is absent from official code
file_indicators: Modified JavaScript files in the Tornado Cash UI codebase containing new or altered network request logic not present in official releases
References to external domains (e.g., attacker-server.com) or URLs not found in the legitimate Tornado Cash frontend source code
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from user browsers to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., domains not associated with tornado.cash or official IPFS gateways) during deposit or withdrawal actions
Outbound network traffic containing encoded deposit notes, private keys, or cryptographic secrets in the request body
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform static analysis of deployed DeFi frontend code to identify unauthorized network requests, especially those triggered during deposit or withdrawal operations. Flag any code that accesses deposit notes or cryptographic secrets and transmits them externally. Monitor network traffic from user browsers for suspicious POST requests to non-official domains, particularly those containing encoded sensitive data. Regularly compare deployed frontend code hashes and file contents to official, uncompromised releases to detect unauthorized modifications or insertions.
